scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Executive summary

Diane, you're measured on cutting the $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit that opens in six months — this proposal is built against those two figures, not against architecture. Your 28 SQL Server instances and 620-VM Hyper-V estate currently sit on that $1,850,000 run rate [PF-1.14: source — buyer-stated figure]; the plan replaces that estate with Google Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL over 24 months for $4,200,000 [PF-2.2: source — programme budget as stated]. [PF-2.11 GAP: no vendor-supplied percentage or dollar reduction to the $1,850,000 run rate has been measured yet; do not infer one from the programme cost alone]. Because your audit window opens in six months, the load-matching and carrier-settlement systems carry the compliance exposure, and any commitment about audit readiness inside that window needs your own confirmation before it ships [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm whether "clean audit" can be promised on this timeline given the migration is still in flight].

What you should expect from the programme: a capability mapping from your current SQL Server/Hyper-V estate to Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, a stated risk treatment for anything that cannot be retired before the audit opens, and a spend trajectory tied to your $1,850,000 baseline rather than to feature claims [PF-1.9: capability — running load-matching and carrier-settlement workloads on managed infrastructure — stated ahead of the product named as its means]. [PF-2.13 GAP: no differentiator over a named alternative has been supplied for this summary — none is claimed here]. [PF-2.4: no proof point or comparable migration reference has been supplied — cut rather than invented].

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| [PF-1.14: source — buyer-stated figure] | PF-1.14 | Confirm $1,850,000 is Diane's own stated figure, not assumed |
| [PF-2.2: source — programme budget as stated] | PF-2.2 | Confirm $4,200,000/2-year figure's source document |
| [PF-2.11 GAP] | PF-2.11 | A measured or targeted reduction percentage/dollar figure against the $1,850,000 baseline |
| [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment)] | PF-2.14 | Confirm whether any audit-readiness date/promise can be stated given the 6-month window |
| [PF-2.13 GAP] | PF-2.13 | A named differentiator this vendor can support versus a named alternative |
| [PF-2.4] | PF-2.4 | A proof point or comparable migration this vendor can actually produce |
